narrows.how: The intrusive-list header family (mk_list/cfl_list foreach, plain and safe, next and prev) is now recognised and lowered from the header's original spelling (gateway 5l). Every other for header keeps rule 10c(3). Not retired.

Part (5) W45-FB-P1-SLICES, backlog half: the FB-BACKLOG-CUSTODY slice has been run as a semantic card with Rust and audited Lean against the re-pinned (046accf6) denominator, every delta attributed; its obligations remain Unknown with the measured blockers registered here. The retry half and parts (1)-(4) are unchanged. Not retired.

registers.title: Backlog OB-2/OB-3 need a wrapper-to-chunk reference relation, return-conditioned clauses and per-element identity; v1 states none
registers.why: W45-FB-BACKLOG-CUSTODY expressed the storage-backlog obligations as checked specifications (providers/quirin-provider-fluent-bit/contracts/fluent_bit/storage_backlog.qcore, contract spec C06.3). OB-2 (no chunk closed while a wrapper refers to it; the -3 arm of sb_append_chunk_to_segregated_backlogs, observed natively as the partial fan-out ASan use-after-free) and OB-3 (at most one wrapper per chunk per queue) relate a wrapper, a queue and a chunk; the v1 vocabulary states only argument and result custody. Measured reach of a relation clause alone in this slice is 0: the chunk is an element of stream->chunks (sb_segregate_chunks) or of a wrapper (cb_queue_chunks), both untracked by the projection, and the failing insertion is inside a loop whose callee has no return-conditioned summary. DISCHARGE: a C09 relation clause (wrapper refers to chunk; close requires no outstanding reference), a return-conditioned clause, and per-element abstract identities for admitted list iterations, with loader, gateway and Lean parity, then the slice as arbiter deciding OB-2 on the -3 arm; any refutation stays a provisional Unsafe, never an upstream defect claim.

registers.title: flb_input_chunk_map's chunk has three dispositions (stored, closed on the routes_mask arm, left open); no v1 mode is faithful, so OB-4/OB-5 stay Unknown
registers.why: W45-FB-BACKLOG-CUSTODY left flb_input_chunk_map undeclared: on success the chunk is stored into the returned input chunk, on the routes_mask allocation failure it is closed (BC-1), and on the other NULL arms it is left open. OB-5 (chunk closed exactly once on a NULL map return; cb_queue_chunks closes it again) and OB-4 are therefore not decidable; BC-1 remains a source-reading candidate. Unchanged between 864c3d97 and 046accf6. DISCHARGE: a per-arm (or per-return) disposition clause in C09 with loader/gateway/Lean parity, or a source argument; then the backlog slice deciding OB-5.

registers.title: Backlog OB-6/OB-7/OB-10: callees release objects reachable from their arguments (wrappers of a queue); v1 Borrowed states nothing about them
registers.why: sb_remove_chunk_from_segregated_backlogs, sb_destroy_backlog(s) and sb_release_output_queue_space free wrappers (and queues) reached through a borrowed context; their checked specifications (all Borrowed) are not established by the bodies, whose element releases refuse as unresolved identities. OB-6 (no wrapper used after a callee frees it), OB-7 (eviction retires every wrapper before the close) and OB-10 (teardown) need a clause for objects released through what an argument reaches (P-B08-SHALLOW is the current premise). DISCHARGE: such a clause with parity, or a container-ownership relation for list elements, then the slice as arbiter.

registers.title: Backlog OB-9 needs ChunkIO return-code summaries (cio_chunk_up_force CIO_OK/CIO_ERROR/CIO_CORRUPTED/CIO_RETRY) and the uncontracted cio_chunk_lock/cio_error_get/cio_chunk_get_real_size
registers.why: sb_segregate_chunks' end states per chunk (OB-9) depend on ChunkIO return codes; cio_chunk_lock, cio_error_get and cio_chunk_get_real_size are uncontracted in the slice. Facts belong in qcore-provider-chunkio. DISCHARGE: ChunkIO declarations read against their bodies (in qcore-provider-chunkio) and a return-code-conditioned vocabulary, then the slice deciding OB-9.

registers.title: Backlog OB-1 (a wrapper is linked into exactly one queue): the link is now modeled (rule 10d), the leg fails on the byte counter's indirect access and no clause states 'exactly one queue'
registers.why: Before the merge of W45-FB-RETRY-LIFETIME, sb_append_chunk_to_segregated_backlog was provisional Unsafe on the unmodeled mk_list_add publication (MK-LIST-ADD-BORROWED-PUBLICATION). On the merged tree rule 10d models the link and withdraws that leak; the function's checked specification (all Borrowed) is still not established, on one indirect access: the saturation test reads backlog->ins->fs_backlog_chunks_size (OB-8, FB-BACKLOG-ACCOUNTING). OB-1's uniqueness half ('exactly one queue') is stated by no clause. DISCHARGE: the counter's read admitted (typed chain through a borrowed formal) and a membership-uniqueness clause, then the slice as arbiter for OB-1.

registers.title: Intrusive-list iteration (gateway 5l) rests on stated premises; 43 element and 34 header leaves stay refused
registers.why: Gateway constraint 5l admits mk_list/cfl_list headers and container_of element reads under four premises stated, not proved: P-ILI-BODY (checked lexically), P-ILI-UNTRACKED (an element is not an identity the body tracks; the lexical guard declines a function where one call receives both &X->... of a possibly tracked X and the iterated head; linking through a wrapper call is P-B08-SHALLOW), P-ILI-CALLEE-FRAME (a callee handed the container does not unlink the protected node; OB-7 depends on it) and P-ILI-BRACED. Rule 4 added no refusal in the corpus or the slice (17 plain bodies with an unlink or release call; the two read release another object or unlink a second link; 15 not read individually). After the card, 43 element-read braced leaves and 34 list-header for-loop leaves remain in the corpus (from 326 and 269), declined by the guard, an untyped head chain or an unbraced body. DISCHARGE: per premise, a model of the callee frame or a measured guard refinement with its re-pin; per residual leaf class, an admission with its own measurement.

registers.title: mk_http_error: descriptor from open() on the custom-error-page arm is never closed (provisional Unsafe candidate)
registers.why: W45-FB-BACKLOG-CUSTODY's declaration reader exposes, in lib/monkey/mk_server/mk_http.c (pinned corpus), a leak of the descriptor fd opened at :1301 and neither closed nor stored before the return at :1315 on the custom-error-page arm; the source's own comment reads 'This fd seems to be leaked'. It is the card's one added leak after its refused-call hand-on repair; unit mk_server/mk_http.c moves Unknown -> provisional Unsafe. Not an upstream defect claim. DISCHARGE: a native observation with a control on a bound build, or a refuting source argument.

registers.title: Rule 10d refuses unlinking an entry this function did not publish; it blocks the backlog's retirement legs (OB-3, OB-7, OB-10) and 17 corpus leaves in 14 teardown functions
registers.why: sb_remove_chunk_from_segregated_backlog and sb_destroy_backlogs unlink wrappers (queues) that another function published (sb_append_chunk_to_segregated_backlog, sb_allocate_backlogs); W45-FB-RETRY-LIFETIME's rule 10d refuses 'unlink by mk_list_del of X, which this function has not published'. W45-FB-BACKLOG-CUSTODY's safe-iteration admission makes 17 such element unlinks reachable in 14 corpus teardown functions (mk_rconf_free, mk_vhost_destroy, flb_input_chunk_destroy, ...), each an exchange for an earlier refusal, fail-closed. DISCHARGE: an unlink of an element of a container the caller owns or borrows, stated against the container's membership (a caller-side publication premise or a container-element identity), with parity and a corpus re-pin.

notes: MK-LIST-ADD-BORROWED-PUBLICATION: the refused-call hand-on repair (gateway 5l clause 5) withdraws its four standing leaves (mk_rconf_read, mk_vhost_create, mk_vhost_set_property, mk_vhost_set_single) to Unknown; none is discharged. Not retired by this card.
